transcript:
Meeting header: Date/time: 2025-03-12 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~48 minutes, Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Acme Security Lead), Tom Alvarez (Acme ML Eng), Priya Rao (Acme CISO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Quick sync to move through security checklist items for the pilot; focus on SSO integration, audit logs format and retention, SOC2 artifacts, and optional dedicated/VPC deployment details.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still a good time?
[00:06] Jenna Park: Yep, all good on our side, thanks.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Awesome. So quick agenda: SSO next steps, audit logs/retention, SOC2 docs, and any blockers for the pilot. Luis will run through sample logs and how we store/export them.
[00:20] Luis Romero: Hi all. I'll start real quick. For the pilot we're running a dedicated sandbox cluster; logs are emitted to our audit pipeline and we can stream them to an S3-compatible endpoint or push via syslog. The log format right now is JSON with fields for request_id, user, route, model_version, tokens_in/out, and error codes.
[00:40] Tom Alvarez: Sorry, can you repeat the fields? We're particularly trying to map to our internal SIEM schema.
[00:44] Luis Romero: Yeah, request_id, principal (the user or service), timestamp, model, route, input_size, output_size, latency_ms, quota_bucket, and any error stack. There might be some downstream name differences, we can map.
[01:00] Tom Alvarez: Got it. Does the payload include prompt content by default?
[01:05] Luis Romero: By default we redact PII and we can configure prompt retention: for this pilot we've got two options — full prompt logging (if you want to send to a private S3 in your VPC) or redacted hashes only. We should not be storing raw prompts in Redwood-hosted S3 unless you opt in.
[01:28] Jenna Park: That's good. Our baseline policy says we cannot have plaintext prompts stored outside our VPC. So we need an option to push logs to our S3 in the same account or have an on-prem export.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Totally understood. We have two approaches: 1) Redwood pushes logs to an Acme-owned S3 bucket (we support cross-account role), or 2) you run the Private deployment (VPC) where logs never leave your network and we provide a private control plane. For the pilot, cross-account S3 export is the fastest.
[02:00] Priya Rao: On the SOC2 front, can you share the report and the scoping? We need to validate controls around access management and encryption.
[02:08] Maya Chen: Yes. We'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and the control matrix. That's in the next steps. Note that our dedicated clusters are covered under the SOC2 scope too — I'll attach the scoping doc.
[02:20] Jenna Park: And pen test? Do you publish pen-test results or a summary?
[02:25] Luis Romero: We have third-party pen tests; we can't share raw findings but we can share an executive summary and remediation timelines. We also have an internal vulnerability disclosure program and bug-bounty summary.
[02:40] Tom Alvarez: For SSO mapping, we use SAML with attribute mappings: email, groups, and a custom attribute for role_id. We need to make sure the token mapping into Redwood's RBAC supports group-based policies.
[02:55] Maya Chen: That works. Redwood supports SAML and OIDC. For SAML we map attributes to RBAC groups; Luis, can you note the attributes needed?
[03:05] Luis Romero: Yeah. We'll need email, groups, and an optional role attribute. We can also support SCIM for provisioning if you want automated user sync.
[03:15] Jenna Park: SCIM would be helpful but not blocking for the pilot.
[03:18] Priya Rao: One more on retention: what are your retention controls and deletion timelines? We need a policy we can reference for GDPR/data residency.
[03:28] Luis Romero: Default retention for logs in Redwood-hosted buckets is 90 days, with configurable retention down to 7 days or up to multi-year on dedicated. For data deletion, we support on-demand deletion requests and a documented deletion API. If you put logs in your S3, you control lifecycle.
[03:45] Maya Chen: Also note we have options for token redaction and KV cache redaction; KV cache is not persisted outside of the node unless you opt into snapshotting.
[03:55] Tom Alvarez: Can you clarify encryption at rest keys? We use a customer-managed KMS if we go with dedicated or the private deployment. For hosted, is CMK available?
[04:05] Luis Romero: For Redwood-hosted we use provider-managed keys by default, but for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and HSM integrations for on-prem. We'll include the KMS notes in the doc pack.
[04:20] Jenna Park: Good. About audit logs format — we need an example file so our SIEM team can map fields.
[04:26] Luis Romero: I'll send a sample JSON and a CSV transform. Note that some fields may be noisy, but we'll work with you to map the canonical fields.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Small note on compliance: when you evaluate SOC2 artifacts, we can't provide raw user-level logs from other customers, but we'll provide architecture diagrams, control descriptions, and sample (sanitized) logs from the pilot environment.
[04:50] Priya Rao: Understood. Also curious — what about retention for embeddings and whether they're considered PII? Our legal says embeddings derived from PII may still be sensitive and need retention controls.
[05:02] Luis Romero: Yes, embeddings are treated as derived data; retention is controlled the same as prompts/input. We can configure embeddings to be ephemeral or stored in your tenancy depending on the workload. For the pilot we can make them ephemeral or store in your VPC.
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: For the SSO integration call — who's the right contact on Redwood?
[05:22] Maya Chen: I'll own the coordination and Luis will lead the technical. So Maya and Luis from Redwood, Tom and Jenna + maybe your IdP engineer on the Acme side.
[05:32] Jenna Park: Okay. For the audit log export, can you support pushing logs to our Splunk intake via HTTP events?
[05:38] Luis Romero: We support Splunk HEC and generic webhook push; we can also do S3 delivery. We'll send configuration snippets.
[05:46] Maya Chen: Quick timeline check — are we still on track to finish pilot eval by end of month?
[05:50] Tom Alvarez: Yes, assuming no big blockers on SSO or audit exports. Implementation of SAML might take a few days but not more than a week.
[06:00] Priya Rao: If we find a critical control gap, what is your escalation path? We need an SLA for security incidents during the pilot.
[06:07] Maya Chen: We'll provide a security incident response addendum for the pilot and our security on-call escalation. We can commit to notify within predefined windows; I'll include the SIRP summary.
[06:20] Jenna Park: Can you confirm if logs contain full prompt text by default? I want that in writing.
[06:26] Luis Romero: By default no — prompts are redacted. Full prompt retention is opt-in and requires configuration to export to your own storage. We'll document that clearly.
[06:36] Tom Alvarez: Good. Also, any PCI or HIPAA scope? Our initial use-case is not PCI, but may include PHI later.
[06:44] Maya Chen: We have HIPAA controls and a BAA option for customers with PHI use cases; we'll surface the BAA process in the doc pack. For PCI, we can discuss scoping but it's generally out-of-scope unless you have cardholder data flows into prompts.
[06:58] Luis Romero: One thing I want to call out: latency/throughput for audit-heavy workloads. If you enable full logging to external sink synchronously, there's a small added tail latency; we can do async delivery to avoid that. For the pilot we recommend async delivery to your S3.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Okay, quick recap of next steps: Maya to send SOC2 and network diagram by Friday (2025-03-14); Luis to send sample logs and Splunk config by 2025-03-19; Tom to send audit schema and retention windows by 2025-03-18; Jenna to confirm RBAC groups by 2025-03-17. Set SSO integration call for 2025-03-17.
[07:44] Jenna Park: Sounds good. Anything else from Acme?
[07:47] Tom Alvarez: No, that's it. We'll get the schema over.
[07:50] Priya Rao: Thanks, appreciate the clarifications.
[07:52] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.

Auto-actions (verbatim): Share SOC2 report; sample audit logs; schedule SSO call; provide Splunk/S3 config snippets.

End of transcript.
